newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - January 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - January 8.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Wednesday:

Former Transport Minister Michael Lowry, who resigned last year after admitting reports that a department store owner paid for his house repairs, has opened a campaign to save his political career and his North Tipperary seat.
A police intervention squad was within seconds of storming Mountjoy prison to rescue four warders held hostage by six prisoners.
The Cabinet is to rubber stamp the appointment of Bob Collins as Director-general of the nation's RTE broadcasting authority.
Agricutlure Minister Ivan Yates may go to Egypt to press for the reversal of a new ban on live Irish beef exports imposed because of the BSE scare.
Rock Band U2 unveiled its new single, Discotheque, on Iirsh radio on Tuesday night. It is from a forthcoming new album entitled Pop.
